The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(5\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(2x)) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(2x)) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{(2x)^{2}-1}}\cdot (2x)^{′} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}-1}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{10}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
